**Required materials:**

1. Oatley, Chapter 12 — *A Society-Centered Approach to Monetary and Exchange-Rate Policies*
2. Bearce, David H., and Kim-Lee Tuxhorn. 2017. "[When Are Monetary Policy Preferences Egocentric? Evidence from American Surveys and an Experiment](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12235)." *American Journal of Political Science* 61 (1): 178–193. *(PDF on Canvas)*
3. {{< fa headphones >}} [*The Indicator* (Planet Money) — The Mighty US Dollar](https://www.npr.org/2022/09/28/1125771498/the-mighty-us-dollar-encore)

::: {.callout-tip}
## In class today
- Opening **writing prompt**
- Who wins and loses from a strong vs. a weak currency — the preference map
- The three society-centered models: **electoral**, **partisan**, and **sectoral**
- The Phillips curve as the incumbent's lever; the *franc fort* puzzle
- Case workshop: Germany vs. Greece under one ECB policy
- **Student-led article presentation** and discussion
:::
